title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The new RuleSnoozeEndpoint allows an org-wide snooze (user_id=None, which mutes the rule for ALL users per the RuleSnooze model docstring 'Null user_id value means snoozed for all users') whenever the rule has no owner/team. In can_edit_alert_rule, when user_id is None and rule.owner is falsy, the function falls through and returns True with no role/permission check. Combined with ProjectAlertRule

findings.explanation: The new RuleSnoozeEndpoint allows an org-wide snooze (user_id=None, which mutes the rule for ALL users per the RuleSnooze model docstring 'Null user_id value means snoozed for all users') whenever the rule has no owner/team. In can_edit_alert_rule, when user_id is None and rule.owner is falsy, the function falls through and returns True with no role/permission check. Combined with ProjectAlertRulePermission (POST scope_map: project:write/project:admin/alerts:write) and ProjectPermission.has_object_permission (only requires project access), any project member with alerts:write can create a RuleSnooze with user_id=None that silences the alert for every user in the organization — a privilege escalation beyond the per-user 'me' snooze path. This is newly exposed by the PR.

evidence.content:
"""
    Duration an issue alert or metric alert is snoozed for a user.
    Null `until` value means snoozed forever.
    Null `user_id` value means snoozed for all users.
    """

findings.suggested_fix: Require an elevated role (e.g. organization admin/owner or a dedicated alerts:admin scope) for the org-wide snooze path (user_id is None) instead of allowing any project member with alerts:write. In can_edit_alert_rule, when user_id is None, verify the user has an org-level admin role (or that the rule's owner team grants admin) before returning True, rather than defaulting to True when rule.owner is falsy.
